goal: Decide the next state of one Rule 30 cell from its neighbourhood, so every row of the automaton can be replayed and checked.

app.name: rule-thirty-cell
app.title: Rule 30 cell
app.purpose: Decide the next state of a Rule 30 cell from its left neighbour, itself and its right neighbour.

meanings.on: the cell is black in the next row
meanings.off: the cell is white in the next row

rules.why: rule30-lexlean/src/Core.lex.tex: rule a b c = bxor a (b || c), so 100 gives 1
rule30-lexlean/src/Core.lex.tex: with a off, rule is b || c, so 010 and 011 give 1
rule30-lexlean/src/Core.lex.tex: with a off, rule is b || c, so 001 gives 1

app.otherwiseWhy: rule30-lexlean/src/Core.lex.tex: bxor a (b || c) is 0 for 000, 101, 110 and 111

properties.why: Core.lex.tex: with a and b on, bxor true true is false, so 110 and 111 give 0
a white neighbourhood stays white, the background of the Rule 30 diagram

stakeholders.name: Researcher
stakeholders.text: Studies the Rule 30 sequence for Prize Problem 1 and needs every cell of every row to be the one the rule gives.

stakeholders.name: Proof engineer
stakeholders.text: Extends the LexLean and Lean 4 formalization and needs the cell rule to stay the one Core.lex.tex and the prize kit define.

concerns.name: Agreement with the prize kit
concerns.text: The local rule is the one Rule30PrizeKit defines, as rule30-bridge/Rule30Bridge.lean connects every paper theorem to Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Prize.

components.name: Rule30PrizeKit
components.text: The Rule 30 Prize kit, Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Prize, whose definitions the bridge module ties the LexLean theorems to.

components.name: r30 command surface
components.text: bin/r30: status, frontier, theorem add, check, verify and axioms, also served as an MCP server.

threats.name: Rule drifts from the prize kit
threats.text: The cell table differs from the Rule 30 the prize kit defines, so a replayed row is not the automaton the prize asks about.

control.name: Bridged to the prize kit
control.text: Rule30Bridge.lean proves every LexLean paper theorem against the kit definition, and all eight neighbourhoods are acceptance examples.

threats.name: Classical choice in a proof
threats.text: A proof of the rule depends on Classical.choice, which the repository forbids in its authored proof surfaces.

control.name: Choice forbidden
control.text: The kernel axiom audit accepts only propext and Quot.sound, and a source check rejects classical constants.

threats.name: Boundary cells guessed
threats.text: A caller asks about a cell at the edge of a finite row and supplies a neighbour that is not in the row.
threats.accepted: The app answers one neighbourhood exactly; the convention for cells beyond a finite row belongs to the caller that builds the row.

quality.text: Each of the eight neighbourhoods of three cells is an acceptance example, so the table is checked row by row against Core.lex.tex.
quality.measureText: Of the eight three-cell neighbourhoods, those no example states.
